whatYouSee: The heart points to the right and the stomach gas bubble and the organs are all flipped to the opposite side in a complete mirror image of normal.
whyItMatters: It is usually harmless but spotting it prevents diagnostic errors and missed one-sided disease. Paired with primary ciliary dyskinesia it becomes Kartagener syndrome.
treatment: No treatment is required for the mirror anatomy itself; associated conditions such as Kartagener syndrome are managed on their own.
takeaway: A heart pointing right with every organ flipped is situs inversus totalis.
